name: Domain research and planning
summary: Domain knowledge base, 135 canonical invariants, 500-feature list, Kyle's rulings, tech stack.

name: Schema at parity with the invariants
summary: Close the 80 open invariants in seven waves. Wave 1 landed as v5.4.2-19. Kyle's 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-15 answers unblock tax, franchise fees, the PGA billing side and waves 4, 6 and 7. Wave 2: v5.4.2-22 (periods, close snapshot, GL mapping, aging) landed 2026-10-16. v5.4.2-23 (cash: reversals, positions, per-line application, overpayment credits) is through four review rounds; Kyle answered K-10 on 2026-10-21 (a refund is its own movement) and Ryan dropped the refunded/donated statuses and chose a new credit for a refund that comes back after escheat. Round 4 found six narrower holes (refund trees, the overpayment credit's split of a take-back, escheat corner cases); r5 is next. v5.4.2-24 (unmatched cash, agency pledges) follows. Wave 3 started while waiting: v5.4.2-25 (disputes: the dispute law and tariff rule family, the dispute record, the readers) and v5.4.2-26 (collections decisions: every notice, late fee, disconnect and referral cites a recorded decision; field verification with supervisor overrides) are drafted and tested; both go to review after -23 r3.
basis: Measured: about one medium schema patch per working day including review; about 8 patches left plus decision waits.

name: Scenarios and testing strategy
summary: Write the 200-390 scenarios the core must pass, have Kyle check the numbers, and choose how they become tests.
basis: Claude drafts at schema pace; the limit is Kyle checking the dollar figures and the 200-390 scenario count.

name: Core build plan
summary: Break the C# core into ordered build phases, each with its scenarios as the finish line. Choose the launch feature set.
basis: Judgment: one planning document plus the launch-feature cut.

name: Platform foundation
summary: AWS environments, infrastructure as code, CI/CD, staff login, the .NET solution, and database access that sets the tenant on every connection.
basis: Judgment at AI pace; depends on the login and hosting decisions.

name: Core billing engine (C#)
summary: The billing engine and API, built in sub-phases planned in P3. Each sub-phase finishes when its scenarios pass.
basis: Schema pace used as the stand-in (no C# written yet). Re-measure after the first core sub-phase.

name: Frontend hardening and integration
summary: Take the prototype (36 screens on made-up data) to production: real login, roles, the generated API client, error states, accessibility.
basis: Judgment at AI pace; runs alongside the core once the API exists.

name: Integrations
summary: The outside systems a utility cannot run without. Vendors depend on the first customer's contracts.
basis: Judgment at AI pace; generic adapters only, vendor-specific work happens during onboarding.

name: Test data and release testing
summary: A synthetic utility with a year of history, end-to-end tests, and a full billing-run load test. The fixtures are built from P2 onward; this phase is the final pass.
basis: Judgment: final pass, since fixtures are built during P2 and P5.

name: Security and operations readiness
summary: Backups and disaster recovery, monitoring, an outside penetration test, incident runbooks, and SOC 2 groundwork.
basis: Calendar-bound: the outside penetration test and recovery drills are booked with vendors.

name: First customer: conversion and setup
summary: Starts at the ready-to-onboard date. Convert the customer's data from the old system, load their tariffs and ordinances, and train their staff.
basis: Calendar-bound: the customer staff and old-system vendor set the pace.

name: Parallel billing runs
summary: Bill the customer's real cycles on both systems and reconcile every difference. 2 to 4 monthly cycles.
basis: Calendar-bound: two to four of the customer's monthly billing cycles.

name: Go-live and stabilization
summary: Cut over, then close support for the first live billing cycles.
